title: Bias and Fairness in Large Language Models: A Survey

bias_targets.methodology: Embedding-based metrics (e.g., WEAT, SEAT) using cosine similarity, probability-based metrics (e.g., masked token prediction, pseudo-log-likelihood) using counterfactual pairs like Winogender and WinoBias, and generated text-based metrics including distribution analysis and lexicon scoring (e.g., Gender Polarity).

Probability-based pseudo-log-likelihood comparisons using stereotype and anti-stereotype sentence pairs (e.g., CrowS-Pairs, StereoSet), and evaluating generated text for toxicity, sentiment, and demographic representation disparities.
Masked token predictions, counterfactual sentence likelihoods, and question-answering benchmarks (e.g., BBQ, UnQover) to measure stereotypical associations and disparate performance.

Counterfactual sentence pairs (e.g., WinoQueer) and question-answering tasks to assess stereotyping, as well as text generation prompts to measure toxicity and derogatory language against the LGBTQ+ community.
Question-answering benchmarks containing ambiguous contexts (e.g., BBQ) and counterfactual sentence pairs (e.g., CrowS-Pairs, PANDA) designed to detect stereotyping and disparate system performance.
Counterfactual unmasked sentence pairs and question-answering tasks (e.g., BBQ) to evaluate misrepresentation, stereotyping, and exclusionary norms.
Inference tasks (e.g., Bias NLI), masked token templates, and question-answering frameworks (e.g., UnQover) to measure stereotypical associations and polarity differences.
Counterfactual sentence pairs (e.g., CrowS-Pairs) and question-answering tasks (e.g., BBQ) to assess stereotyping.
Evaluated through sentence pairs and question-answering benchmarks (e.g., BBQ, CrowS-Pairs) to detect stereotyping and allocational harms.
